headline: Spanish Cognates Foundation
threshold: Use familiar Spanish-English word families without trusting spelling alone. Practice pronunciation, stress, agreement and false friends through contextual reading and original responses.

lessons.title: Recognize familiar words at a hotel
lessons.objective: Recognize familiar words at a hotel: Similar spelling is a useful clue, not proof of meaning.
lessons.focus: Recognize familiar words at a hotel

words.es: Busco un hotel cerca del hospital.
words.en: I am looking for a hotel near the hospital.

words.es: Pregunto si aceptan un animal pequeño.
words.en: I ask whether they accept a small animal.

words.es: La radio está en la habitación.
words.en: The radio is in the room.
I review the plan for tomorrow.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing recognize familiar words at a hotel. Similar spelling is a useful clue, not proof of meaning. Check the whole sentence and say Spanish vowels clearly. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Find information with -ción
lessons.objective: Find information with -ción: Many English -tion nouns have a related Spanish -ción form.

words.en: I need information about the station.

words.es: La dirección está en el mensaje.
words.en: The address is in the message.

words.es: Una conversación con Ana aclara la situación.
words.en: A conversation with Ana clarifies the situation.

words.es: La organización ofrece clases de educación para adultos.
words.en: The organization offers adult education classes.

words.es: La comunicación por teléfono es clara.
Anoto la información y confirmo la dirección.
words.en: I write down the information and confirm the address.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing find information with -ción. Many English -tion nouns have a related Spanish -ción form. Learn each word with its meaning; the written accent marks stress. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Make a decision with -sión
lessons.objective: Make a decision with -sión: Related English -sion nouns often end in Spanish -sión.

words.es: Tenemos una sesión para elegir un programa de televisión.
words.en: We have a session to choose a television program.

words.es: La versión nueva incluye una revisión del horario.
words.en: The new version includes a review of the schedule.

words.es: La decisión depende del tiempo disponible.
words.en: The decision depends on the available time.

words.es: Esta ocasión permite escuchar opiniones distintas.
words.en: This occasion allows us to hear different opinions.

words.es: Nuestra conclusión es probar la versión corta.
words.en: Our conclusion is to try the short version.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing make a decision with -sión. Related English -sion nouns often end in Spanish -sión. Double consonants and accents do not always match; check the actual word. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Describe a community with -dad
lessons.objective: Describe a community with -dad: Many English -ity nouns correspond to Spanish -idad or -dad nouns.

words.es: La universidad prepara una actividad para la comunidad.
words.en: The university is preparing an activity for the community.

words.es: Hay una posibilidad de participar el sábado.
words.en: There is a possibility of participating on Saturday.
In fact, we need more volunteers.

words.es: La necesidad principal es mejorar la calidad del servicio.
words.en: The main need is to improve the quality of the service.

words.es: Una tarjeta confirma la identidad de cada participante.
words.en: A card confirms each participant's identity.

words.es: La comunidad decide repetir la actividad.
words.en: The community decides to repeat the activity.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describe a community with -dad. Many English -ity nouns correspond to Spanish -idad or -dad nouns. These nouns are usually feminine; learn la with the word. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Explain a routine with -mente
lessons.objective: Explain a routine with -mente: Many Spanish -mente adverbs relate to English -ly forms.

words.en: I normally arrive at class early.

words.es: Generalmente leo lentamente la primera página.
words.en: I generally read the first page slowly.

words.es: La profesora explica claramente el ejemplo.
words.en: The teacher explains the example clearly.
I especially practice the new words.

words.es: No repito exactamente el mismo ejemplo.
words.en: I do not repeat exactly the same example.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explain a routine with -mente. Many Spanish -mente adverbs relate to English -ly forms. The adjective base may change; similar-looking adverbs can still differ in meaning. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Describe people with -oso
lessons.objective: Describe people with -oso: English -ous adjectives often have Spanish relatives in -oso.

words.es: Nuestro grupo visita un museo famoso.
words.en: Our group visits a famous museum.

words.es: Un niño curioso hace una pregunta.
words.en: A curious child asks a question.

words.es: Un vecino generoso paga la visita.
words.en: A generous neighbor pays for the visit.

words.es: Al principio estoy nervioso porque no conozco al grupo.
words.en: At first I am nervous because I do not know the group.

words.es: El guía dice que ese camino es peligroso.
words.en: The guide says that path is dangerous.

words.es: Al final compartimos un almuerzo delicioso.
words.en: At the end we share a delicious lunch.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describe people with -oso. English -ous adjectives often have Spanish relatives in -oso. Use -osa, -osos or -osas when needed for agreement; this is a clue, not a universal conversion rule. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Choose something práctico
lessons.objective: Choose something práctico: Many English -ic or -ical adjectives have a related Spanish -ico form.

words.es: Buscamos un servicio práctico para el barrio.
words.en: We are looking for a practical service for the neighborhood.

words.es: El transporte público tiene un precio económico.
words.en: Public transportation has an economical price.

words.es: El plan básico incluye una visita al centro médico.
words.en: The basic plan includes a visit to the medical center.

words.es: Un viaje típico dura veinte minutos.
words.en: A typical trip lasts twenty minutes.

words.es: Pregunto si el servicio está disponible hoy.
words.en: I ask whether the service is available today.
We choose the most practical option.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing choose something práctico. Many English -ic or -ical adjectives have a related Spanish -ico form. Match gender and number, and keep the written accent when the word has one. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Plan a cultural event
lessons.objective: Plan a cultural event: Many English and Spanish adjectives share -al.

words.es: El festival cultural empieza el viernes.
words.en: The cultural festival starts on Friday.

words.es: Una artista local trae material para la clase.
words.en: A local artist brings material for the class.

words.es: Usamos luz natural para ver los colores.
words.en: We use natural light to see the colors.

words.es: Cada persona explica su proyecto personal.
words.en: Each person explains their personal project.

words.es: La información general aparece en la entrada.
words.en: General information appears at the entrance.

words.es: La presentación final es el domingo.
words.en: The final presentation is on Sunday.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing plan a cultural event. Many English and Spanish adjectives share -al. Spanish adjectives in -al normally keep the same form for masculine and feminine; add -es for the plural. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Connect familiar verbs to actions
lessons.objective: Connect familiar verbs to actions: English -ize words can have Spanish relatives in -izar, but do not invent a verb from a spelling rule.

words.es: Vamos a organizar una visita al centro.
words.en: We are going to organize a visit to the center.

words.es: Necesito utilizar el calendario para preparar el viaje.
words.en: I need to use the calendar to prepare the trip.

words.es: Antes de reservar, debemos analizar el precio.
words.en: Before reserving, we must analyze the price.

words.es: Quiero confirmar la fecha con Marta.
words.en: I want to confirm the date with Marta.

words.es: El sábado podemos visitar el museo.
words.en: On Saturday we can visit the museum.

words.es: Si cambia el horario, tenemos que cancelar la reserva.
words.en: If the schedule changes, we have to cancel the reservation.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing connect familiar verbs to actions. English -ize words can have Spanish relatives in -izar, but do not invent a verb from a spelling rule. Learn the infinitive and a complete example. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Check gender instead of guessing
lessons.objective: Check gender instead of guessing: A familiar-looking noun still needs its Spanish gender and stress.

words.es: El programa muestra un mapa del barrio.
words.en: The program shows a map of the neighborhood.

words.es: Hay un problema con el sistema.
words.en: There is a problem with the system.

words.es: Una persona explica el tema en otro idioma.
words.en: A person explains the topic in another language.

words.es: Miro una foto de la entrada.
words.en: I look at a photo of the entrance.

words.es: El mapa confirma dónde está la oficina.
words.en: The map confirms where the office is.

words.es: Resolvemos el problema y guardamos la foto.
words.en: We solve the problem and save the photo.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing check gender instead of guessing. A familiar-looking noun still needs its Spanish gender and stress. El problema and el sistema are masculine despite ending in -a; do not infer meaning or gender from spelling alone. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.
